text:
kai: FYI I pushed a draft dashboard for prefetch/kv cache guardrails — focused on per-model/per-route/per-tenant hit-rate + token-saved delta. Wanted quick feedback before I pin it to the runtime ops board.

maya: nice, can you show the query for the tenant slice? want to check acme-corp numbers.

kai: sure, the core hit-rate is: 
```promql
(sum by(model, tenant) (rate(prefix_cache_hits[5m]))) / (sum by(model, tenant) (rate(prefix_cache_requests[5m])))
```
and token-saved is computed as: 
```promql
sum by(tenant, model) (rate(prefix_cache_hits_tokens_saved[5m]))
```

sam: looks good. Observability nit: add a 95p token-saved per-request metric, we care about tail customers.

nora: ran the dashboard for last 7d — spotted a ~18% drop in hit-rate for model redwood-serve-3 at route `/v1/chat/generate` for tenant acme-corp around 03/11 02:00 UTC. Token-saved also fell even though absolute request volume rose.

kai: hmm that aligns with a kernel change we rolled to the serving fleet ~02:50 — switched to the new batching heuristic (batcher-v2) + kernel selector tweak. Might be a regression in how we compute prompt key normalization at the batch boundary.

leo: @kai can you attach the profiling snippet that shows KV cache lookup times? wondering if extra string normalization added latency which could change key collisions.

kai: pasted profiler output: 
```text
KVLookup: median 0.9ms -> 1.7ms after change
KeyNormalize: median 0.2ms -> 0.9ms
BatchBoundaryKeyRewrite: 0.0ms -> 0.5ms
```
so yes, extra work per-request. Could explain throughput/backpressure pattern causing fewer prefix hits (clients hit new cold paths).

grafana-bot: [alert] prefix-cache-hit-drop (sev: warning) triggered for redwood-serve-3 / tenant=acme-corp at 1711185000.

maya: thanks — for mitigation, we should probably: 1) revert the batcher tweak for 24h on the affected subset, 2) add a dashboard panel with "prefetch warmup coverage" (fraction of requests served from warmed kv vs total), 3) add an automated sampling trace when hit-rate drops >10% for a tenant.

sam: +1. Also add a per-route cold-start heatmap binned by sequence-length and model param count — helps explain cases where longer contexts fail to match cached prefixes.

nora: on the dashboard I added a lightweight playbook panel with these thresholds and who to page: infra-oncall if tenant drop >20% or token-saved delta < -10k tokens/hour.

kai: will add the sampling trace hook. Proposed sample rule: when tenant hit-rate change >= 8% and token-saved delta <= -5k, capture 200 request heads (inputs) and KV keys, sanitized.

leo: small privacy note — KV keys include hashed prompt fragments. Make sure the sample redacts any PII per our sampling runbook (we should store only the normalized key and customer id).

kai: yes, hash + retention 7d. I'll add that to the dashboard notes.

maya: one more ask — expose model variant toggles on the dashboard so product can quickly switch to a quantized variant with higher hit affinity if needed.

kai: okay. Action items: 
- kai: add sampling trace + redact rules + rollback toggle (ETA 2h)
- maya: add 95p token-saved panel + model-variant toggle (ETA 4h)
- sam: add cold-start heatmap query & per-route seq-length slice (ETA EOD)
- nora: update playbook thresholds and alert text (ETA 1h)

nora: noted. I also exported a CSV of tenant slices and sent to #eng-sre for the oncall play.

infra-bot: deployment window scheduled: canary revert (batcher-v1) for 10% of fleet at 1711203600 if changes validated.

sam: let's validate against the dashboard using the same 5m aggregation window. If hit-rate for acme-corp recovers within 20m on the canary, we can expand.

kai: I'll follow up in 30m with a canary validation report. Thanks for the rapid feedback everyone :thumbsup:

leo: thanks — LGTM.
